decision.location: Introduction and Methods RQ1–RQ3, TablesVII–X and final Conclusion; raw preflight0177
decision.quote:
original study provided the extracted CFG information for
replicating their work but not the Java source code of the
analyzed methods, which we retrieved from the corresponding
project repositories on GitHub. We also had to develop the
classification models that we then used for predicting MRs,
because also they were not shared by the authors of the original
paper. We conducted the first step to check whether we can
re-create the classifiers with as good quality as in the original
study and to prepare for the next steps by building our own
classifiers based on features extracted from the CFGs derived
from the source code of methods.
The next two steps of our study aim at exploring the
transferability and generalizability of the PMR method. In the
second step, we checked whether classifiers generated from
Java code perform equally well when applied to Python and
C++ code. Therefore, we created two datasets, one comprising
100 methods in Python and other one comprising 100 methods
in C++. Both sets of methods implemented the exact same
decision.reason: Full current Methods/RQ1explicitly reuse the original100Java-method DOTgraphs (DSJK), independently reconstruct their source-derived graphs (DSJV), and retrain models with a different implementation. This is original-observation reanalysis, not new Java methods merely because code was retrieved again. RQ2/RQ3also construct newPython/C++code artifacts implementing the same100functions; their language-specific structures and learned models are new code observations and genuine generalization evidence, while not independent new underlying mathematical functions. These are two substantive empirical workflows in a single record: original-data implementation checks and new-artifact generalization. The paper and its exclusive codebook schema provide no rule selecting one record-level type or allocating the distinct workflows to separate target-level records. Calling all steps replication would erase the direct original-graph reanalysis; calling all reproduction would erase new code artifacts. Retain actual hybrid data/scope ambiguity. Conditional on a replication schema, the stated original JavaPMRcomparison is successful and fixed-model zero-shot transfer failure is a separate extension; it does not establish failed original cross-language transfer that the original never empirically reported. Conditional on reproduction, original-code numerical recovery and alternative-implementation robustness require separate axes. Do not transfer a single categorical outcome before type is resolved. This limit follows the fully read available design, not missing local text or provider failure.
